facts.F15: Question 1 (preservation law): retire feature A's Refinement call of the move law. Delete RefinementRulesSeeTheMoveArchUnitTest, RefinementPatternRoles and RefinementStringsTheMoveRenames, and drop the rename-list use in RefinementLivesInItsModuleArchUnitTest. Reason: the move is complete and feature B pins every type to its new namespace, so a law that compares old and new sight has no old side left, and a Refinement call kept as a move-complete check would be a second owner next to the C1 oracle. NamespaceMoveLaw, PatternDeclaration and PatternRoleMap stay: PlatformLaneRulesSeeTheMoveArchUnitTest still uses them.
facts.F16: Question 2 (C1 oracle): one new file RefinementRulesNameOnlyTheModuleArchUnitTest owns the whole check. It reads every rule constant of the test assembly by reflection and sweeps every string literal of the test project sources for the four old forms (the old Implementation and Interfaces Refinement namespaces, as a plain name, a regex alternative or a group member, and the two old folder paths). A hit is allowed only in a declared measurement file (RefinementMembership, RefinementMembershipArchUnitTest, RefinementLivesInItsModuleArchUnitTest, RefinementUnitTestsBesideTheModuleArchUnitTest, NamespaceMoveLaw and the oracle itself); that list is compared both ways, so a listed file with no hit fails until it is removed. It also asserts that each Refinement rule pattern still matches a Refinement type in its new namespace, so narrowing cannot make a rule blind. Made-up offenders are fixtures declared to the oracle.
facts.F17: Question 3 (C2): RefinementModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest on ModuleRules, modelled on PromisesModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest and LicensingModuleBoundariesArchUnitTest, with ModuleWording Refinement and the API. R-R1 TypesLiveInTheirLayer per layer (Domain, Application) with the former home set to the whole Services pattern; R-R2 DomainReachesOnlyTheKernelAndTheBaseLibrary; R-R3 DomainIsReachedFromOutsideOnlyBy with an empty list and legal callers by namespace (API, composition root, Refinement Application); R-R4 ApplicationIsReachedFromOutsideOnlyBy with an empty list and legal callers API and the composition root; R-R5 Application outbound forbidden targets (EF Core, Data, API, module Adapters, Tracker integration, update code) with an empty list; R-R6 OutboundEdges into Access, Organisation set-up, the Platform lane and repositories along an inline list measured from the IL by the acceptance designer. Expected list from the design record: VoterIdentityResolver to Access, RefinementCalendar to the blackout service and the clock, SleYardstickResolver to the clock, RefinementCadenceCalendar to WeeklyRecurrence, RefinementList to IWorkItemRepository, RefinementViewQuery and SizingLogCommands to ISizingLogRepository; the IL measurement wins over this expectation. Every list holds full type names, is compared both ways and only shrinks. Falsifiers: per rule and per list position a made-up type in a fixture namespace, in the style of ModuleRulesCatchANewOffenderArchUnitTest; each failure names the edge in Refinement wording.
facts.F18: Question 4 (RefinementModuleArchUnitTest): it stays, with its PortFileTypes exclusion. The new set covers layers and edges only. It does not hold the static-ness of the settings validator, resolution, cadence arithmetic and need band, their Services-Implementation reach, the read path calling no writing repository member, the append-only sizing log, the votes controller or the migration cascades. C1 narrows only its three per-type patterns (resolution, cadence calendar, need band) to Modules.Refinement. The exclusion stays because the types under test and the port types share one Application namespace.
facts.F19: Claim to checker: every claim is a finite set comparison over compiled IL or test sources, checked by native NUnit architecture tests through the real ModuleRules port. No state machine, temporal, fairness or proof claim exists, so Quint, TLA+/TLC and Agda are not applicable and no model file is delivered. Liveness is not applicable: the checks are synchronous and terminate. Carriers: the existing InboundVerdict, OutboundVerdict, KernelRuleVerdict and IlDependent records; no new carrier. Paradigm object_oriented with the repository's static rule classes; no domain object is added. Property testing: the lists are finite, so native table cases are used, not generators. code-fact was not used; callers were found by text search and the impact is closed by reading the test project.
